thread:
Mira Patel: quick heads-up — we're bringing up the Cobalt customer dialect LoRA on the 13B baseline. Need a short compatibility + quantization scan before we open the canary.
Simon Lee: ok — what are the known gotchas?
Mira Patel: tokenizer: new dialect tokens like `yer`, `yee-ya` are being split into weird subwords, which breaks intent detection. Also saw odd hallucination increase when we run int8 on the merged model.
Cheng Wu: I ran a tiny quickpack (200 samples domain-specific QAs). Commands I used: ```bash
./eval_pack.sh --model merged-cobalt-lora-13b --quant int8 --dataset cobalt_quick200 --out quick200.json
```
Cheng Wu: results: baseline 13B FP16 EM 84.3, merged FP16 EM 83.9 (-0.4). merged int8 EM 81.2 (-3.1). Perplexity drift ~+6%. Weirdly, examples with the `yee-` tokens had >10% drop.
Alex Chen: did you keep tokenizer merges/preset from the LoRA training? If LoRA relied on added special tokens we should preserve them on merge. Merge command I use: ```python
from merge_utils import merge_lora
merge_lora('base-13b', 'cobalt-lora', out='merged-cobalt-lora-13b', preserve_tokens=True)
```
Simon Lee: good call. If tokenizer vocab mismatch -> subword splitting. We should compare token ids for a few example prompts.
Mira Patel: can someone run a token-diff for sample: `yee-ya what's the delta` vs base?
Cheng Wu: ran token diff: base -> ['y', 'ee', '-', 'ya', ...], finetune tokenizer -> ['yee', '-', 'ya', ...]. Merge without preserve_tokens reverted to base splits.
Alex Chen: so two options: 1) keep finetune tokenizer merges on customer env (need ops sign-off), or 2) add simple post-token mapping in preproc for `yee*` family to map to merged tokens. Option 2 low-risk.
Simon Lee: on quant side, can you try per-channel quant (q8) or quant-aware smoothing? int8 is aggressive. Also try KV-cache aware int8 run: `--kv-quantize false` sometimes helps.
Cheng Wu: re-ran with `--kv-quantize false` and q8 per-channel: int8-like speed with EM 82.7 (improvement). Also reduced hallucinations on FAQ prompts.
ops-bot: scheduled a canary slot on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 for 2026-03-22T09:00Z (window 2h) — task id run-2026-03-22-0789.
eval-bot: quickpack summary attached: metrics: {"baseline_fp16_EM":"84.3","merged_fp16_EM":"83.9","merged_int8_EM":"81.2","merged_q8_EM":"82.7","perp_delta":"+6%"} (see quick200.json)
Mira Patel: thanks. Proposed next steps: (1) preserve tokens on customer deploy OR add preproc mapping, (2) run larger quickpack (2k) with q8 + kv-disabled to validate, (3) plan canary in that ops slot if results hold. Who can take (2)?
Alex Chen: I'll kick off the 2k pack and push scripts to /infra/onboard/cobalt/quickpacks. ETA end of day.
Simon Lee: I'll draft release note about token-preserve tradeoffs and fallback mapping.
Mira Patel: great — ping here when 2k results land. :thumbsup:
